1#א: The conclusion of the Gemara on the Mishnah regarding a piece of neveilah, etc. — Chullin daf 100.
1#ב: Tosafot, the Rosh, and the Ran there, from the Mishnah of those that are forbidden, etc., and basar b'chalav, etc. — Avodah Zarah daf 74.
2#_: The Rosh there; and so wrote the Rashba, the Ran, and other poskim. The reason is that the prohibition within it is not worthy of honor. And as for basar b'chalav — if it is worthy of honor it is not nullified — that case is different, because since they were cooked together with one another, the whole reverts to being as one body, as written above in siman 92, seif 4.
3#א: Tur in the name of his father the Rosh, in the name of some who say, there at the end of the chapter of Gid HaNashe; and the Rashba, the Ran, and other poskim; and so wrote the Semak and Sha'ar Dura in the name of an incident that came before Rabbeinu Tam.
3#ג: There; and so wrote the Rashba in Torat HaBayit, and the Ran, of blessed memory.
3#ד: Tur in the name of his father, the Rosh.
4#_: Beit Yosef in the name of a found written source; and Issur VeHeter.
5#_: Tur in siman 114, and Sefer Mitzvot Gadol, Negative Commandment 141, in the name of Rav Yehuda.
6#א: The Rosh at the end of the chapter of Gid HaNashe, from the case of one who crushed nine ants while one was alive, etc. — Makkot daf 16; and in the name of a responsum of the Rif; and in the name of Tosafot; and so wrote the Rashba and the Ran there.
6#ב: The Rosh and the Ran, from that which I cited in siman 99, seif 5.
7#_: The Rosh and the Ran there.
8#_: Hagahot Maimoniyot in chapter 7 of Hilchot Shechita, in the name of an incident that came before Rabbi, etc., from that which I cited above in siman 83, seif 4; (and Hagahot Asheri at the beginning of the chapter of Eilu Tereifot, in the name of Or Zarua).
